note: Generic illustrated anatomy. Boundaries and added internal shapes are approximate, not an MRI atlas. No additional assessment scores.

regions.label: Frontal lobe
regions.where: Front of each cerebral hemisphere.
regions.function: Supports planning and coordinated behavior with other brain networks.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. Follow the blue anterior surface. Named frontal subdivisions have their own colors.

regions.label: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
regions.where: Upper, outer prefrontal cortex.
regions.function: A contributor to executive-control networks for goal-directed tasks.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. This patch marks an approximate teaching location, not a measured functional boundary.

regions.label: Orbitofrontal cortex
regions.where: Underside of the frontal lobe, above the eye sockets.
regions.function: Helps represent expected outcomes and their changing value.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. Rotate toward the underside or isolate this region to see its position.

regions.label: Primary motor cortex
regions.where: Precentral gyrus, in front of the central sulcus.
regions.function: Contributes commands for voluntary movement.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. Compare the orange strip with the sensory strip just behind it. Strips are illustrative.

regions.label: Primary somatosensory cortex
regions.where: Postcentral gyrus, behind the central sulcus.
regions.function: Processes body sensation, including touch and position.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. The yellow strip is posterior to the motor strip; a full body map is not modeled.

regions.label: Parietal lobe
regions.where: Upper posterior cerebrum, behind the frontal lobe.
regions.function: Integrates sensory information and spatial relationships.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. Find the green upper surface behind the sensory strip.

regions.label: Temporal lobe
regions.where: Lateral lower cerebrum, below the lateral fissure.
regions.function: Supports hearing, memory and aspects of language processing.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. The purple side region is a lobe, not one single language or social center.

regions.label: Occipital lobe
regions.where: Back of each cerebral hemisphere.
regions.function: Processes visual information.
regions.look: Geometric teaching boundary on a generic surface, not a registered anatomical atlas. Rotate to the rear to distinguish the occipital lobe from the cerebellum below.

regions.label: Auditory association cortex
regions.where: Upper temporal surface near the lateral fissure.
regions.function: Interpreting sounds and language-related auditory information.
regions.look: A broad superior-temporal teaching patch; not the exact cluster from a study.

regions.label: Visual cortex (medial occipital)
regions.where: Back and inner surface of the occipital lobe.
regions.function: Visual processing within multiple interacting visual areas.
regions.look: A broad medial-occipital teaching patch, not a precise V2 or lingual-gyrus segmentation.

regions.label: Posterior cingulate cortex
regions.where: Inner posterior cortex above the corpus callosum.
regions.function: A contributor to the default-mode network; its roles depend on task and context.
regions.look: A small medial teaching patch, not a precise posterior-cingulate or isthmus atlas parcel.

regions.label: Precuneus
regions.where: Medial parietal surface above the posterior cingulate area.
regions.function: Participates in higher-order visual and awareness-related processing.
regions.look: An approximate medial teaching area.

regions.label: Amygdala
regions.where: Medial temporal region, near the front of the hippocampus.
regions.function: Salience, learning and responses to significant events.
regions.look: Not simply a fear switch; shown as paired schematic structures.

regions.label: Hippocampus
regions.where: Medial temporal region in each hemisphere.
regions.function: Learning, memory and contextual relationships.
regions.look: Curved teaching shape; hippocampal subfields are not individually segmented.

regions.label: Anterior cingulate cortex
regions.where: Medial frontal surface arching above the front of the corpus callosum.
regions.function: Monitoring, regulation and coordination within networks.
regions.look: The cingulate is cortex, not a deep nucleus. This arch is a schematic medial-cortex guide.

regions.label: Insula
regions.where: Cortex buried inside the lateral fissure.
regions.function: Integrates bodily and other salient information.
regions.look: The insula is folded cortex, shown schematically beneath the outer surface.

regions.label: Thalamus
regions.where: Paired structures near the center of the brain.
regions.function: Routing and coordinating sensory and other information.
regions.look: Many thalamic nuclei are simplified into one teaching form per side.

regions.label: Hypothalamus
regions.where: Below the thalamus near the brain base.
regions.function: Homeostatic and hormonal regulation.
regions.look: A small midline teaching form; no hormone concentration is inferred.

regions.label: Periaqueductal gray
regions.where: Around the cerebral aqueduct in the midbrain.
regions.function: Contributes to pain modulation and defensive responses.
regions.look: Highly simplified ring-like guide; not the entire midbrain.

regions.label: Corpus callosum
regions.where: Midline white-matter arch between the cerebral hemispheres.
regions.function: Communication between hemispheres.
regions.look: Two joined schematic halves illustrate a continuous commissure, not measured fiber pathways.

regions.label: Cerebellar vermis
regions.where: Midline portion of the cerebellum.
regions.function: Coordination and regulation within cerebellar networks.
regions.look: Schematic vermis shown separately from cerebellar hemispheres.

regions.label: Ventral striatum / nucleus accumbens guide
regions.where: Ventral forebrain below the caudate head.
regions.function: Reward-related learning and motivated behavior.
regions.look: The small accumbens-centered guide is not the full ventral striatum or a pleasure meter.

regions.label: Caudate nucleus
regions.where: Curved structure around the lateral ventricle, medial to the putamen.
regions.function: Contributes to action selection and learning.
regions.look: A schematic curved nucleus; no neuronal counts or personal volume are represented.

regions.label: Putamen
regions.where: Lateral striatum, outside the caudate and thalamus.
regions.function: Action selection and motor-learning networks.
regions.look: A schematic bilateral shape, distinct from the ventral-striatum guide.

regions.label: Cerebellar hemispheres
regions.where: Below the posterior cerebrum.
regions.function: Coordination, timing and learning in distributed networks.
regions.look: Original licensed surface retained; no precise cerebellar lobular atlas.

regions.label: Brainstem
regions.where: Below the cerebrum, continuous with the spinal cord.
regions.function: Contains pathways and centers supporting essential body functions.
regions.look: General teaching anatomy; not a localization of a respondent’s symptoms.
